reviews.review:
If you like warhammer, then you will like this game.

The story is good, but the final boss is dissapointing, because you don't fight him.

The combat is a combination of a third person shooter and a third person hack and slash.

Character progression is done with new pieces of equipment you obtain the more you advance in the story.

Overall, it's a good game. I hope they make Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 one day.

Unfortunately, this game is not compatible with modern CPUs with more than 8 CPU-cores. Cores need to be deactivated in BIOS.
(crashes on launch)

Edit 08/2024
I have a i9 14900K for some time now. Tried to launch the game again out of curiosity...  It doesn't start.
This """""PC""""" game really doesn't deserve anything more than a thumbs down..
Theres like 0,0000000001% of PC games that behave like this. To many cores = no game.

This review is taken from my website:

So here's the thing: for a buttery smooth first-person rampage you get DOOM; for a third-person one you get Warhammer 40K: Space Marine! Donning a ridiculously over-sized suit of armour left over by a terran space-marine from Starcraft - that no normal human being could stand up in let alone leap about in while killing a gazillion orcs - you set off on a journey through various space-stations and planets doing precisely that. 

Bounding around in chunky funky fashion, you tear your way through five chapters, and 17 missions, while ripping enemies apart in satisfying explosions of shredded orc-flesh with your heavy-duty arsenal of your devastating melee weapon of choice and four ranged ones (or two if you opt to carry the overpowered thing). Level design is quite linear - it's basically one battle after another - but the oozing bloodbath and explosive action that ensues never gets old. Unfortunately the final boss battle got the better of me and I didn't quite finish but other than that, for a mindless romp, the game definitely delivers.
